subject: mathematics
question_text: Three numbers are in G.P. Their sum is 43 and their product is 216. Find the numbers in proper order.

mark_split.label: Take the numbers as a/r, a, ar
Solve for r and list the numbers

recall_prompt: Say how you would set up the three numbers, and say why that choice makes the product easy.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Take the numbers as a/r, a, ar
steps.margin_note: First mark. The choice of a/r, a, ar is the marked move, because r cancels in the product and a = 6 follows in one line.
steps.memory_tip: Three numbers in G.P. with the product given: write a/r, a, ar so the r cancels.
lines: Let the three numbers be  a/r,  a,  ar

recall.must_convey: That the numbers are taken as a/r, a, ar, the product gives a = 6, and the sum gives 6r² − 37r + 6 = 0.
accept: take the numbers as a by r, a and a r
the product is a cubed so a is six
writing them this way makes the ratio cancel in the product
a by r, a, a r ga teesukovali, product lo r cancel
the sum gives a quadratic in r

steps.why: Choosing a/r, a, ar makes the product a³ because r cancels. That gives a immediately and leaves only r unknown in the sum.
common_mistakes: Taking the numbers as a, ar, ar² also works — a³r³ = 216 gives ar = 6 — but a/r, a, ar gives a = 6 directly and is shorter.
Forgetting to multiply the whole sum equation by r before forming the quadratic.

steps.label: Solve for r and list the numbers
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Check both conditions: 1 + 6 + 36 = 43 and 1 × 6 × 36 = 216. Either order is a correct answer.
steps.memory_tip: The two roots 6 and 1/6 are reciprocals, so the same list only reverses.
lines: r = 1/6 gives the same three numbers reversed: 36, 6, 1

lines.text: ∴ the numbers are 1, 6, 36  (or 36, 6, 1 in the reverse order)

recall.must_convey: That r = 6 or 1/6, giving the numbers 1, 6, 36 in one order or 36, 6, 1 in the other.
accept: the quadratic factorises to r minus six into six r minus one
r is six or one by six
the numbers are one six and thirty six
one, six, thirty six vasthai, reverse kuda correct
both roots give the same three numbers in opposite order

steps.why: The two roots are reciprocals of each other, so they give the same three numbers read forwards and backwards. Both orders satisfy the sum and the product.
common_mistakes: Reporting only r = 6 and saying the other root fails.
Splitting the middle term with the wrong signs and getting r = −6.
